ANNEX A ANNEX B FOREWORD

8

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Rotating Machinery Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. This is a comprehensive standard covering generators coupled to internal combustion engines without distinction of output and voltage, with the exception of machines intended for special applications, such as machines for traction vehicles, marine service and air transport.

( Continued on r&d cover )

IS 13364 (Part 1) : 1992
. Indian Standard AC GENERATORS DRIVEN BY RECIPROCAZ'ING INTERNAL COMBUSTION ENGINESSPECIFICATION

PART 1
1 SCOPE

ALTERNATORS RATED UP TO 20 kVA

e) Bxposure

1.1 This standard specifies the requirements for ac generators together with their exciters driven by reciprocating internal combustion engines and generators having outputs up to 20 kVA at specified conditions. 1.2 This standard covers generators with the following excitation systems: a) Direct excitation adopting static exciters (magnetic or electronic); b) Brushless AC exciters; c) DC exciters; and d) Pilot exciters besides exciters in (b) or (c) above. The excitation power in these cases is derived fromthe prime mover of the alternator. The closed loop (involving an automatic voltage regulator) or open loop of excitation control may be used in the excitation systems. 1.3 This standard does not cover generators intended for use in the following special applications. However, machines built to this standard may be adopted with suitable modification for these applications when agreed between the manufacturer and the purchaser/ user: a) Exposure to: 9 abrasive or conducting dust or chemical fumes; ii) combustible dust; iii) dusts/fumes of explosives; iv) flammable gases; v) lint; vi) nuclear radiation; vii) oil vapour; and viii) salt air.

to cooling media where the temperature values depart from those listed in this standard.

h) Where the phase voltages, or currents,
are severely unbalanced.

The AC generator to which this standard applies.

3.2 Rating Numerical values of the electrical and mechanical quantities with their duration and sequences assigned to the machine by the manufacturer and stated on the rating plate forspecified conditions. 3.3 Load All the numerical values of the electrical and mechanical quantities that signify the demand to be made on a 1

3.11 Effkiency The ratio of output power to the input power (expressed

as a percentage): Power output of machine Efficiency = Power output of machine + Power loss in the machine
3.12 Routine Tests

The apparent electric power available at terminals

expressed in volt-amperes or kilovolt amperes together with the specifies power factor, frequency and voltage. 3.5 No Load
The state of a machine rotating at normal speed under

rated conditions but when no output is taken out of it. 3.6 Overload Any load in excess of rated load expressed numerically in per unit or percentage of rated output. 3.6.1 Sustained Overload An overload sustained for a sufficiently long period to affect appreciably the temperature of the machine. 3.6.2 Momentary Overload An overload the duration of which is so short as not to affect appreciably the temperature of the machine. 3.6.3 Balanced Load A symmetrical 3-phase load having equal numerical value of impedance and power factor of load in all the 3-phases. 3.6.4 Unbalanced Load A load having different magnitude and power factor loads in all or any two of the 3-phases. It is normally expressed as ratio of the difference of maximum and minimum line currents to the maximum line current as follows:

Tests carried out on each machine to check the essential requirements which are likely to vary during production. 3.13 Type Tests Tests carried out to provide conformity with the requirements of this standard. These are intended to prove the general qualities and design of a given type of machine. 3.14 Voltage Terms These terms describe a generator under the control of its normal excitation and voltage regulation system. 3.14.1 Rated Voltage (UN) The line-to-line voltage generator at rated output. 3.143 at the terminals of the

No Load Voltage (UJ

The line-to-line voltage at the terminals of the generator at rated frequency and at no load, 3.143 Range of Voltage Adjustment (AU,> Range of maximum possible upwani and downward adjustment of voltage a&generator terminals (Umax and bin) at rated frequency, for all loads between no load and rated load and within the agreed range of power factors. 3.14.4 Inherent Voltage Regulation (R,U) The maximumchange involtage expressed as percentage of the rated voltage, when the load changes from rated load at rated voltage, speed and power factor to any lower load, including no load, without change in speed and excitation current, taking into account the effect on governor and automatic voltage regulation. 3.143 Transient Voltage Deviation (R,u)

3.7 Duty Statement of the load including no load, rest and deenergized period to which the machine is subjected including their duration and sequence in time. 3.8 Duty Type Aconventional periodic duty consisting of one or more sets of loads remaining constant for the durations specified. 3.9 Thermal Equilibrium
The state

Maximumdeviationofvoltageafterasuddenspecified load change from a voltage previous to steady state level at rated speed and specified power factor. 3.14.6 Voltage Recovery Time (tu) The. time interval from the point when the voltage departs from the specified steady state voltage regulation band after a load change until the voltage again returns to and remains within this band. 3.14.7 Voltage Regulation Characteristics (-) Curves of terminal voltage as a function of load current or KVA at given power factor and rated frequency. 2

reached when the observed temperature rises of the several parts of the machine do not vary by more than 2OC over a period of one hour.
3.10 Excitation Voltage

The voltage marked on the rating plate of a machine and required for excitation at rated output.

IS 13364 (Part 1) : 1992 3 14.tI Voltage Modulation (Modulation Amplitude) <b, v Voltage modulation is a quasi-periodic voltage variation about a steady state voltage at frequencies below the fundamental of service frequency expressed as a percentage of the rated voltage at rated frequency and uniform drive. 3.149 Angular Displacement of Polyphase System (W Electrical angular displacement of the generator phase voltage vector relative to the corresponding phase voltage vector of a symmetrical polyphase system (with three phase system 1200 at virtually non-deforming and virtually balanced loads between no load and rated load, expressed in electrical degrees). 3.14.10 Maximum Voltage Unbalance (bv) The maximum voltage unbalance is the ratio of the negative sequence or the zero sequence voltage components to the positive sequence voltage components at no load. 4 SlTR CONDITIONS 7.1 Preferred 4.0 The following shall constitute the normal site conditions. 4.1 Altitude and Temperature Voltages For the purpose of this standard, the preferred voltages shall be in accordance with IS 12360 : 1988. b) the frequency differeing from its rated value by not more than 23 percent, or c) any combination of (a) and (b). In the case of operation at extreme voltage limits, the temperature rise limits specified in 11 shall not exceed by more than 5OC.Machines when operated under the abnormal conditions of voltage and frequency variation may not necessarily have their performace in accordance with this standard. 5 TYPE OF ENCLOSURES For machines covered by this standard, the specification for types of enclosures shall be as given in IS 4691 : 1985. 6 COOLING SYSTEMS The machines covered by this standard shall have one of the cooling systems given in IS 6362 : 1971. 7 PREFERRED AND OUTPUTS VOLTAGES, FREQUENCY

8 IRREGULARITIES 8.1 Non Linear Loads

OF WAVEFORM

a suitable machine from this standard list to meet this duty, based on data supplied by the purchaser.
lOEARTHING

The non linear loads (thyrister drives) introduce har-

monics in the alternator armature current. This in fact disturbs the generator voltage waveform which may lead to malfunctioning of the system and also cause additional heating of the generator rotor. A standard alternator shall supply 20to 4Opercent non linear loads along with conventional loads of 80 to 60 percent depending upon'the design of thyrister panel and alternator parameters. It is recommended that users of alternators will inform the generator manufacturer whenever the thyrister loads or furnace loads are encountered. 9 DUTY
The generators covered by this standard shall be of continuous duty unless specified otherwise by the purchaser.

Earthing of the machine shall be done in accordance with the relevant provisions of IS 3043 : 1987.
11 TEMPERATURE RISE LIMITS

The generators to this standard shall meet the limits of temperature rise covered in IS 4722 : 1992.

12 OVERLOAD
12.1 Momentary Excess Current for Generators

Other duties can be specified as per one of the requirements in IS 4722 : 1992. The manufacturer may select 4

A generator rated in accordance with this standard shall be capable of withstanding for not less than 15 seconds, a current 50 percent in excess of its rated current after having attained the thermal equilibrium corresponding to the rated load, the voltage being maintained as near the rated value as possible consistent with the maximum capacity of the prime mover. The exact value of the voltage is not important.

IS 13364 (Part 1) : 1992

12.2 Exciters The exciters shall be capable of delivering the required excitation current for overloads specified in 12.1.
12.2.1 The exciters shall be rated 1.25 times the full load (rated) conditions.

injurious sparking or injury to the commutator or brushes. 14.2 The slip ring brushes of AC generators should be free of injurious sparking or injury to slip ring or brushes from no load to momentary overload specified in 12. 14.3 Annex B of IS 4722 : 1992 gives details of the grades of sparking that may be used in specifying the degree of sparking.

The user should give complete information on the generators at the time of enquiry. Annex B may be referred for providing such details. 20 TESTS 20.1 General The tests specified in this clause shall normally be carried out at the manufacturer's works. 20.2 Test Certificates 203.1 Unless otherwise specified when inviting tenders, the purchaser, if so desired by the manufacturer shall accept manufacturer's certificate as evidence of the compliance of the machine with the requirements of 12 and 20.4.1 on a machine identical in essential details with the one purchased together with routine tests on each individual machine. In the case when a batch of 10 or more similar machines are supplied on one order, type tests, as specified, shall be made on one of tbese machines, if the purchaser so requires. 20.23 Certificates of routine tests shall show that the machine purchased has been run and found to be electrically and mechanically sound and in working order in all particulars. 20.23 Ifsospecified,wheninvitingtenders,testsshall be carried out at the manufacturer's works in the presence of the purchaser or his representative to ensure that the machine complies in every respect with the requirements of 11,12,21 and 22 at steady state regulation and efficiency. 203.4 Certificates of all type tests together with a record of alterations whether essential or not, which have been made to the machine since the tests were carried out, shall be kept available by the manufacturer for inspection. 20.3 The procedures laid out in IS 7132 : 1973 and IS 7306 : 1974 for testing the generators other than single phase and evaluating the machine parameters will in general apply to the generators covered by this standard. Testing for single phase generators will generally conform to the routine tests covered by 20.4. For single phase generators of the brushless type, circuit characteristic need not be checked. 204 Synchronous 20.41 Type Tests The following shall constitute the type tests: a) Measurement of resistance, b) Phase sequence test (for,3-phase generators only), c) Regulation test, d) Measurement of open circuit characteristic only, 6 Generators

21 HIGH VOLTAGE TEST High voltage test will be conducted on the machine with exciter as per IS 4722 : 1992. 22 INSULATION RESISTANCE TEST The test requirements and the procedure shall be in accordance with IS 4722 : 1992. 23 OVERSPEED 23.1 All machines shall be designed to withstand a speed of 1.2 times the rated speed unless specified otherwise. 23.2 An overspeed test is not normally considered necessary but may be performed when this is specified and has been agreed between the manufacturer and the purchaser at the time of the order. An overspeed test shall be considered as satisfactory if no permanent abnormal deformation is apparent subsequently and no other weakness is detected which may prevent the machine from operating normally and provided the rotor windings after the test comply with the required dielectric tests. The duration of any overspeed test shall be two minutes. 23.3 Due to settlings in laminated rotor rims, laminated poles held by wedges or by bolts,`etc, a minute

IS 13364 (Part 1):1992 permanent increase in the diameter is natural and not to be considered as an abnormal deformation indicating that the machine is not suitable for normal operation. 24 UNBALANCED LOAD Unless otherwise specified, three phase synchronous generators of ratings up to 20 kVA shall be capable of continuously o rating on an unbalanced load (as defined in 36.4 p" of 25 percent with none of the phase currents exceeding the rated current. The temperature rise limits specified in IS 4722 : 1992 may exceed by 1CPCwhen generator operates under such conditions. The voltage regulation under the above condition will not apply. 25 SHORT CIRCUIT CURRENT Unless otherwise specified, the peak value of the short circuit current for synchronous machines, in the case of short circuit on all phases during operation at rated voltage, shall not exceed 15 times the peakvalue or 21 times the rms value of the rated current. The check may be carried out by calculation or by means of a test at a voltage of 50 percent of the rated voltage or above. 26 INSTANTANEOUS SHORT CIRCUIT WITHSTAND TEST FOR AC GENERATORS 26.1 The short circuit test for ac generators shall be carried out only at the express request of the purchaser made at the time ofthe order. Inthis case, the test shall be carried out on the machine running on no load with an excitation corresponding to the rated voltage, unless otherwise agreed upon. In no case shall the test be carried out with an excitation greater than that corresponding to 1.05 times the rated voltage. 26.1.1 This voltage may be reduced by agreement between manufacturer and the purchaser in order to take into account the impedance of the transformer which may be placed between the generators and the system. In the latter case, it may be requested that the test be made on the site with the over excitation device in service. The short circuit shall be maintained for 3 sec. 26.2 The test is considered satisfactory if no harmful deformation occurs and if the requirements of the high voltage test are met after the short circuit test. 27 PARALLEL OPERATION 27.1 If desired by the purchaser, the manufacturer shall provide means to ensure stable parallel operation of the generator with other generating sets or with another source of supply, also ensuring correct sharing of the reactive power. 28 OTHER APPLICABLE STANDARDS IS 900 : 1%5 INDIAN

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded oft` in accordance of significant with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Mark

The use of the Standard Mark IS governed by the provIsIons of the Bureau of Indian StarrdurdsAct,. 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked producrs are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. .
